subject: Renewal + co-purchase: GPU bucket add & PO amendment

Subject: Renewal options + extra GPU bucket during co-term

Connor,

We’re starting budget prep for our Jan renewal (contract CORD-2026-045) and want to explore adding a dedicated GPU bucket to our renewal so that the new capacity is co-termed with the existing commitment. Primary asks from procurement and infra:

- +40 GPUs (A100-equivalent) reserved as a separate bucket for batch training/ingestion windows
- Throughput guarantee for the bucket (we care about 95th percentile tail latency for inference lanes)
- Prefer to co-term the added capacity to our existing renewal date (2027-02-01) rather than extend the term

Procurement asked whether this will be a PO amendment or a new PO and what the billing cadence would look like if we do a co-purchase as part of the renewal. Can you share a draft amendment and an example billing schedule?

Thanks,
Sarah

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal options + extra GPU bucket during co-term

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and timing. High level: co-purchasing the extra GPU bucket as a PO amendment that co-terms to your renewal date is viable and is the path most customers take to keep a single renewal cadence. Attached are: 1) a draft PO amendment that adds a "Reserved GPU Bucket" line item and 2) a sample billing schedule with two cadence options (monthly amortized or quarterly installments).

Key points:
- Contract mechanics: we will amend the existing contract (no change to the base term end date) and add a separate SKU for the reserved bucket. The amendment will reference the existing PO number so procurement gets a single invoice flow.
- Throughput SLA: we can add a 95th percentile latency target for your inference lanes tied to the reserved pool. SLA exceptions and credits will be limited to when the bucket is fully utilized; we recommend adding a burst pool of 10% of committed GPUs to handle spikes.
- Billing cadence:
  Option A — Monthly amortized: spread the one‑time hardware reservation fee across the remaining months in the current term (lower monthly hit).
  Option B — Quarterly installments: equal payments per quarter, aligned to your fiscal calendar (simpler for procurement).

Attached: PO_Amendment_CORD-2026-045-v1.pdf, billing_schedule_v2.xlsx.

Next steps: if procurement prefers one of the billing options, we’ll produce a redlined amendment for legal and a DocuSign envelope for signature. Marissa — looped you in for pricing confirmation. Aditya — quick legal look on the amendment language when you have a moment.

Regards,
Connor O'Brien

Connor — pricing sign-off below. If we fold the 10% burst pool into the committed bucket, the effective committed quantity becomes 44 GPUs (40 + 10% burst included in the SKU price). That lets procurement approve faster because they don't have to agree to an explicit add-on later.

Pricing summary to show in amendment: 
- Reserved GPU Bucket: 44 GPUs (A100-equivalent) — annualized rate prorated to co-term with existing renewal.
- One-time reservation fee: $88,000 (amortizable).
- Monthly equivalent if amortized: $7,333/month for the remaining 12 months.
- Quarterly installments option (preferred by Cordata): $22,000 per quarter for 4 quarters.

SLA note: we can include a 95th percentile latency target for the inference lanes backed by a service credit of up to 5% of the bucket fee for sustained breaches (standard cap applies). Aditya — I’ve attached amendment_redline.docx with markup for the SLA and PO reference.

Once Aditya confirms legal, I approve sending the DocuSign packet to procurement@cordata.com and we should include the HubSpot deal id in the amendment header.
